findings.claim: In SpanFlusher.join(), when the deadline expires the `break` exits the per-process loop before terminate() runs for the current and remaining flusher processes, leaving them running after join returns during shutdown/rebalance.

The isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) guard before process.kill() in the restart path (_ensure_processes_alive) is always False for spawn-context SpawnProcess objects, so hung or unhealthy processes are never killed before replacements start. The pre-PR code called kill() unconditionally.

In join(), terminate() sits behind the same isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) check, which is always False for SpawnProcess, so flusher processes are never terminated on shutdown or rebalance.
_create_process_for_shard (lines 127-132) has no callers in src/ or tests/ and only delegates to _create_process_for_shards, so it is dead code.
Having both _create_process_for_shard and _create_process_for_shards, with near-identical names, is confusing.
In test_basic in test_consumer.py, the added time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched to a no-op earlier in the test, so it does not give the flusher time to process.
test_flusher_processes_limit asserts only internal attributes and does not check that segments from all shards are flushed across multiple processes. No test covers the restart/kill path.

The CLI default for --flusher-processes is 1 (one process for all shards), while SpanFlusher and ProcessSpansStrategyFactory default max_processes to None (one per shard). This forces a single process, and tests exercise only the per-shard path.

The docstring 'Creates one process per shard' does not match the default deployment, where the CLI default of 1 runs all shards in one process. The comments at lines 178 and 235 also do not match the code.
max_processes is normalised twice, self.max_processes is kept only for the test, and _create_processes is a 2-line wrapper with one caller.

--flusher-processes is a plain int with no lower bound: 0 silently means one process per shard, and a negative value gives a negative num_processes and an empty process_to_shards_map, causing a KeyError during shard distribution.
submit() loops over one SpansBuffer per child process, calling get_memory_info() and record_stored_segments() N times against the same Redis cluster on the consumer main thread.
The spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce timer (line 199) uses tag key 'shards', while the other metrics in the same flush loop (lines 185, 195, 244) use 'shard'.

The 'shard' tag value at lines 185 and 195 is a comma-joined list of a process's shards, which changes on rebalance and has high cardinality. Line 244 tags a single int under the same key, and existing buffer metrics use 'shard_i'.
Several new comments (lines 59, 82, 92, 241, 336) restate the code.
The `if not process: continue` guard in _ensure_processes_alive can never be true, because self.processes only holds started Process or Thread objects, which are always truthy.
The hasattr/isinstance anti-pattern guidance added to CLAUDE.md (lines 448-458) is unrelated to the span-flusher change.

Each process's SpansBuffer computes ceil(max_flush_segments / len(assigned_shards)) over only its own shard subset, so spans.buffer.max-flush-segments becomes a per-process budget. Total flush per cycle and the backpressure threshold therefore scale with process count.
